newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key US T-bond edges up on bargain-hunting in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key US T-bond edges up on bargain-hunting in Tokyo.

text.p: The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond extended its gains by Tokyo afternoon on Thursday on short-covering following sharp overnight losses, traders said.
The firm tone in the T-bond futures market also contributed to gains in the cash market, they said.

"Japanese and Asian bargain-hunters were detected to have bought actively on dips," said a trader at a Japanese securities house. "But heavy purchases are likely to be limited as the key (30-year bond) yield approaches 6.5 percent."
The key 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond was at 98-28/32, yielding 6.59 percent, against 98-10/32 in New York.
In New York on Wednesday, Treasuries fell sharply as foreign investors dumped long positions on concerns that the recent heavy inflow of international capital may be over.

Traders said the climate of the market is gradually weakening after the recent falls, with prices falling below various key technical support levels. The market's attention is on U.S. consumer price data due for release at 1330 GMT.

"All kinds of speculation, including scepticism about Japanese institutional investors' appetite for Treasuries, seem to have hurt the mood," the trader said. "But I think they are sticking to their attitude of buying Treasuries on dips."
